data.name: Ashba
data.gender_notes: Ashba is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'ashba' meaning 'horse'. In Islamic tradition, it symbolizes strength, power, and courage. The name Ashba carries the meaning “Fierce horse” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ashba usually hope their child will grow to embody fierce horse and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Ashba is a name with deep spiritual significance. It represents the mystery and power of the night, and the protection and nurturing energy it provides. It is a reminder of the beauty and wonder of the natural world, and the cycles of life and death.
data.etymology: Ashba belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fierce horse.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ashba total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_arabic.name: أشباء
in_arabic.meaning: أشباء تعني الأشخاص أو الأشياء التي تشبه بعضها
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم أشباء مشتق من الفعل 'أشبه' الذي يعني التشابه أو المماثلة. في اللغة العربية، يُستخدم هذا الاسم للإشارة إلى الأشخاص أو الأشياء التي تشبه بعضها في الصفات أو المميزات. وقد وردت كلمة 'أشباه' في القرآن الكريم في سورة الأنعام آية ١٢١، حيث يقول الله تعالى: 'وما ذهب عنها من شيء فإنه يلق إليه ومن يلق إليه فإنه يلق في جهنم ساءت مثواه'، والآية تشير إلى أن الأشباه يلقون في جهنم إذا لم يكونوا على الطريق الصحيح. واسم أشباء يعتبر من الأسماء ذات المعنى العميق في الثقافة الإسلامية.

in_urdu.name: اشباء
in_urdu.meaning: اشباء کا مطلب ہے ایسے لوگ یا چیزیں جو ایک دوسرے کی طرح ہوں
in_urdu.long_meaning: اشباء نام عربی زبان کے الفعل 'أشبه' سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے مماثلت یا تشابه. اردو میں، اس نام کا استعمال ان لوگوں یا چیزوں کے لیے کیا جاتا ہے جو ایک دوسرے کی طرح ہیں ان کی صفات یا خصوصیات میں. اسلامی تقویم میں، اس نام کا ذکر اہم سمجھا جاتا ہے کیونکہ یہ نام ذات الٰہی کی مختلف صفات کی یاد دلاتا ہے.

in_hindi.meaning: अशबा का अर्थ है ऐसे लोग या चीजें जो एक दूसरे जैसे हैं
in_hindi.long_meaning: अशबा नाम अरबी भाषा के क्रियापद 'أشبه' से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है समानता या सादृश्य। हिंदी में, इस नाम का प्रयोग उन लोगों या वस्तुओं के लिए किया जाता है जो अपनी विशेषताओं या विशेषताओं में एक दूसरे जैसे होते हैं। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, इस नाम का महत्व इस्लामी परंपरा में इसकी जड़ों के कारण बहुत अधिक माना जाता है।

in_english.name: Ashba
in_english.meaning: Ashba means people or things that resemble one another
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ashba is derived from the Arabic verb 'أشبه' (ashabaha), which means to resemble or be similar. In Islamic tradition, this name refers to people or things that share similar qualities or characteristics. The root of this name is found in the Quranic context where 'ashbah' (أشباه) is mentioned, implying those who are alike in their actions or fate. The name Ashba carries significant spiritual connotations, symbolizing unity and similarity among individuals. Historically, this name has been used across various Muslim cultures to signify the bond between similar entities.

data.cultural_impact: In Arabic culture, the naming of children after animals is a common practice. The name Ashba not only pays homage to this tradition but also to the significant role horses played in both Islamic and Arabian history. Horses played a vital role in various aspects - from warfare to transportation - making them an essential part of the Islamic and Arabian heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, the name Ashba symbolizes the human qualities and virtues associated with horses. Prominently, horses are characterized by strength, power, agility, and determination, all of which are considered desirable qualities in the Islamic context. Metaphorically, the name Ashba serves as a reminder for the individual to embody these virtues and strive towards self-improvement and growth. The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) stated that a true believer is like a horse: when the rider falls asleep, the horse continues its journey and reaches its destination; similarly, the believer, even when he overlooks his obligations, is propelled towards good by faith.
